A.subject: Physics
A.text: A satellite of mass m is launched vertically upwards with an initial speed u from the surface of the earth. After it reaches height R(R = radius of the earth), it ejects a rocket of mass (m/10) so that subsequently the satellite moves in a circular orbit. The kinetic energy of the rocket is ( G is the gravitational constant; M is the mass of the earth):
A.sol_text:
Solution:

[Diagram shows satellite at Earth surface with initial velocity mu, moving to height 2R]

(1/2)mu² + (-GMm/R) = (1/2)mv² + (-GMm/(2R))
⇒ (1/2)m(v² - u²) = (-GMm)/(2R)
⇒ v = √(u² - GM/R) ...(i)

v₀ = √(GM/(2R))  ∴ v_rad = (m×v)/(m/10) = 10v

∴ (9m/10) × √(GM/(2R)) = (m/10) × v_r ⇒ v_r² = 81(GM/(2R))

∴ KE_rocket = (1/2) × (m/10) × ((u² - GM/R)100 + 81GM/(2R))

= (m/20) × 100(u² - GM/R + 81GM/(200R))

= 5m(u² - 119GM/(200R))

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A particle of mass m is dropped from a height h above the ground. At the same time another particle of the same mass is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with a speed of √(2gh). A.sol_text:
Answer : (4)
Solution:
Time of collision

Speed of (A) just before collision v₁↓ = gt₀ = √(gh/2)

And speed of (B) just before collision v₂↑ = √(2gh) - √(gh/2)

After collision velocity of centres of mass

V_cm = [m(√(2gh) - √(gh/2)) - m√(gh/2)]/(2m) = 0

So from there, time of fall t'

⇒ 3h/4 = (1/2)gt'^2

⇒ t' = √(3h/(2g))

Diagram shows:
s₁ = h/4
s₂ = 3h/4

⇒ t₀ = h/√(2gh) = √(h/(2g))
∴ s₁ = (1/2)gt₀² = (1/2)g · (h)/(2g) = h/4
∴ s₂ = 3h/4

B.text: A person goes to a mall and sees an escalator which was moving upward at a constant rate. He walks up the escalator at a rate of 1 step per second and finds that he reaches the top while he took twenty steps. B.sol_text:
Speed of escalator = v
Total steps in case-1 = 20 + v × 20

Total steps in case-2 = 32 + v(32/2)
= 32 + 16v

20 + 20v = 32 + 16v
12 = 4v
v = 3 steps/s

∴ Total steps = 20 + 60 = 80

Answer : 80.00

Total entropy change

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let z be a complex number satisfying the equation |z − (1 + i)|² = 2 and ω = 2/z, then the locus traced by ω in the complex plane, is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (1)
Solution:
Answer (1)
From given equation is |(x + iy) − 1 − i)|² = 2
⇒ (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 2
⇒ x² + y² = 2(x + y)

⇒ 2(x + y)/(x² + y²) = 1 ..............(i)

Let ω = α + iβ = 2/z = 2/(x + iy) = 2(x − iy)/(x² + y²)

⇒ α = 2x/(x² + y²), β = −2y/(x² + y²)

Now α − β = 2(x + y)/(x² + y²) = 1 [From Equation (i)]

⇒ Locus of ω(α, β) will be x − y = 1

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The number of ways of choosing five distinct numbers from the first 18 natural numbers such that any two chosen numbers differ by at least 2, is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
Let a₁ < a₂ < a₃ < a₄ < a₅ be the five chose numbers. Consider the numbers (b₁, b₂, b₃, b₄, b₅) = (a₁, a₂ − 1, a₃ − 2, a₄ − 3, a₅ − 4). Then b₁, b₂, b₃, b₄, b₅ are five distinct numbers from the first fourteen positive integers. Conversely, from any five distinct numbers b₁ < b₂ < b₃ < b₄ < b₅ we can reconstruct (a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, a₅) = (b₁, b₂ + 1, b₃ + 2, b₄ + 3, b₅ + 4) to obtain five numbers satisfying the conditions of the problem. Thus we found a one-to-one mapping between the set of five numbers satisfying the given conditions and the set of five distinct numbers from the first fourteen positive integers. Therefore the answer is (14 choose 5) = 2002
